Title: Verify application starts successfully
Preconditions: User has a valid environment to run the application
Steps:
1. Launch the application. 2. Observe the application's startup process.

Test Data: None required
Expected Result: The application starts without errors and is ready for use

Title: Verify application context loads correctly
Steps:
1. Start the application. 2. Verify the application's context is loaded.

Test Data: None required
Expected Result: The application's context is loaded successfully and is accessible

Title: Verify application fails to start with invalid Spring Boot configuration
Preconditions: Application is deployed in an environment with missing or corrupted Spring Boot configuration files
Steps:
1. Remove or corrupt the 'application.properties' or 'application.yml' file in the deployment environment. 2. Attempt to start the application. 3. Observe the startup behavior.

Test Data: Corrupted 'application.properties' file with invalid syntax or missing required properties (e.g., database configuration).
Expected Result: Application fails to start and logs an error indicating invalid or missing configuration. No functional UI or API endpoints are available.

Title: Verify application fails to start with missing or invalid dependencies
Preconditions: Application is deployed in an environment where required dependencies (e.g., database, external services) are unavailable or misconfigured
Steps:
1. Disable or misconfigure the database connection in the deployment environment. 2. Attempt to start the application. 3. Observe the startup behavior.

Test Data: Database service is stopped or credentials are invalid in 'application.properties'.
Expected Result: Application fails to start and logs an error indicating dependency failure (e.g., database connection refused). No functional UI or API endpoints are available.

Title: Verify application rejects invalid command-line arguments during startup
Preconditions: Application is configured to accept command-line arguments for customization (e.g., port, profile)
Steps:
1. Start the application with an invalid command-line argument (e.g., '--server.port=abc'). 2. Observe the startup behavior.

Test Data: Command-line argument: '--server.port=invalid'.
Expected Result: Application fails to start and logs an error indicating invalid command-line argument. No functional UI or API endpoints are available.

Title: Verify application fails to start with insufficient system resources
Preconditions: Application is deployed in an environment with insufficient memory or disk space
Steps:
1. Deploy the application in an environment with critically low memory or disk space. 2. Attempt to start the application. 3. Observe the startup behavior.

Test Data: Environment with less than 100MB of free memory or disk space.
Expected Result: Application fails to start and logs an error related to resource constraints (e.g., OutOfMemoryError). No functional UI or API endpoints are available.

Title: Verify the application starts successfully with no configuration errors
Preconditions: Application is deployed and server is running
Steps:
1. Access the application URL in a web browser. 2. Observe the landing page or login screen.

Test Data: N/A
Expected Result: The application loads without errors, and the landing page or login screen is displayed to the user.

Title: Verify the application handles missing configuration gracefully
Preconditions: Application is deployed with a missing or invalid configuration file (e.g., `application.properties` or `application.yml`).
Steps:
1. Start the application server. 2. Check the server logs for startup errors. 3. Attempt to access the application URL in a web browser.

Test Data: Missing or empty configuration file
Expected Result: The application fails to start gracefully, logs a clear error message about the missing configuration, and does not expose sensitive information to the user.

Title: Verify the application handles extremely large configuration values
Preconditions: Application is deployed with a configuration file containing extremely large values (e.g., a 10,000-character string for a property).
Steps:
1. Start the application server. 2. Check the server logs for startup errors or warnings. 3. Attempt to access the application URL in a web browser.

Test Data: Configuration file with a property value of 10,000 characters (e.g., `app.description=very_long_string...`).
Expected Result: The application either rejects the large value with a clear error message or truncates it without crashing, and the application remains accessible.

Title: Verify the application starts successfully without errors
Preconditions: The application is deployed and the server is running
Steps:
1. Access the application URL in a web browser. 2. Observe the application's landing page or login screen.

Test Data: N/A
Expected Result: The application loads successfully, displaying the landing page or login screen without any error messages or crashes.

Title: Verify the Spring application context loads without errors
Preconditions: The application is built and ready to start
Steps:
1. Start the application using the command line or IDE. 2. Monitor the application logs for startup completion.

Test Data: N/A
Expected Result: The application starts without throwing any exceptions, and logs indicate successful context loading (e.g., 'Started OfferBazarApplication in X seconds').

Title: Verify Maven Wrapper downloads and uses the specified Maven version (3.9.9) and distribution type (only-script)
Preconditions: Clean environment with no existing Maven Wrapper or local Maven installation
Steps:
1. Navigate to the project directory. 2. Run './mvnw --version' (or 'mvnw.cmd --version' on Windows). 3. Observe the output for Maven version and verify the distribution type.

Test Data: wrapperVersion=3.3.2, distributionType=only-script, distributionUrl=https://repo.maven.apache.org/maven2/org/apache/maven/apache-maven/3.9.9/apache-maven-3.9.9-bin.zip
Expected Result: Maven version 3.9.9 is reported, and only the script (not full distribution) is downloaded and used for builds.

Title: Verify the project builds successfully with Spring Boot 3.3.4 and Java 17
Preconditions: Java 17 installed and set as default JDK
Steps:
1. Navigate to the project directory. 2. Run './mvnw clean install'. 3. Observe the build output for success/failure.

Test Data: Spring Boot version 3.3.4, Java version 17
Expected Result: Build completes successfully without errors, and the generated artifact is compatible with Spring Boot 3.3.4.

Title: Verify Lombok is excluded from the final build artifact
Preconditions: Project built at least once (target directory exists)
Steps:
1. Navigate to the project directory. 2. Run './mvnw clean package'. 3. Inspect the generated JAR file (e.g., 'offer.bazar-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar') using 'jar tf target/offer.bazar-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar'. 4. Search for Lombok-related classes.

Test Data: Lombok dependency with <optional>true</optional> and exclusion in spring-boot-maven-plugin
Expected Result: No Lombok classes are present in the final JAR file.

Title: Verify the application starts on the specified port (8082)
Preconditions: No other service running on port 8082
Steps:
1. Start the application using './mvnw spring-boot:run'. 2. Check the logs for 'Tomcat started on port(s): 8082'. 3. Access 'http://localhost:8082/actuator/health' and verify a successful response.

Test Data: server.port=8082
Expected Result: Application starts successfully on port 8082, and the health endpoint is accessible.

Title: Verify the application connects to the PostgreSQL database using the specified URL, username, and password
Preconditions: PostgreSQL server running on localhost:5432 with a database named 'offerbazar' and user 'postgres' with password 'noq@dm1n'
Steps:
1. Start the application using './mvnw spring-boot:run'. 2. Check the logs for 'HikariPool-1 - Starting...' and 'HikariPool-1 - Added connection'. 3. Verify no connection errors or authentication failures are logged.

Test Data: spring.datasource.url=jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/offerbazar, spring.datasource.username=postgres, spring.datasource.password=noq@dm1n
Expected Result: Application successfully connects to the PostgreSQL database without errors.

Title: Verify Hibernate updates the database schema on startup (ddl-auto=update)
Preconditions: PostgreSQL database 'offerbazar' exists but is empty (no tables)
Steps:
1. Start the application using './mvnw spring-boot:run'. 2. Connect to the PostgreSQL database using a client (e.g., psql). 3. Run '\dt' to list tables. 4. Verify that tables corresponding to JPA entities are created.

Test Data: spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update
Expected Result: Database schema is updated with tables for JPA entities, and no existing data is lost (if tables existed).

Title: Verify the JWT secret and expiration values are loaded correctly
Steps:
1. Start the application using './mvnw spring-boot:run'. 2. Use a REST client to call a secured endpoint (e.g., login). 3. Inspect the generated JWT token and verify its expiration time matches the configured value (86400000 ms = 24 hours). 4. Verify the token can be validated using the secret 'test-secret'.

Test Data: jwt.secret=test-secret, jwt.expirationMs=86400000
Expected Result: JWT tokens are generated with the correct secret and expire after 24 hours.

Title: Verify Spring Security logs are set to DEBUG level
Steps:
1. Start the application using './mvnw spring-boot:run'. 2. Attempt to access a secured endpoint without authentication. 3. Check the logs for detailed Spring Security debug messages (e.g., 'Security filter chain', 'Authentication attempt').

Test Data: logging.level.org.springframework.security=DEBUG
Expected Result: Detailed debug logs from Spring Security are visible in the application logs.
